$GOOGL is now discussing deals to extend their memory LTAs through 2035 from KeyBanc channel checks. 

Samsung already has 70% of their capacity allocated through 2031, and this move would suggest a more durable cycle for $MU, $SKHY, and the others. 

They also expect HBM prices up 80% to 100% in the Q1 2027. 

Having all your capacity potentially allocated out into 2035 via LTAs would ease a lot of memory durability fears.

@aleabitoreddit Fresh copium dopamine hit from Serenity post on a day my port gets blasted
@aleabitoreddit If $SIVE doesn't end up being the sole laser provider for Ayar, does this change possible upside in 2027 or 2028?

Nobody said $SIVE was going to be the sole laser provider for Ayar for all generations. 2nd gen Supernova was 16x wavelength that they confirmed Sivers.

Ayar is expected to do multi-vendor for lasers, would be stupid not to. Originally disclosed suppliers were $LITE, $MTSI, and $SIVE, but there's probably only a few companies that can do this new design. 

For their new demonstration at OCP it's 8x 200mW range, $LITE is probably the closest one technologically to Ayar's OCP announcement, with 8x 250 mW demonstrated at ECOC just last month that they're targeting availability later in 2027. 

I don't see anything where $MTSI has demonstrated remotely similar capabilities yet. Macom were saying they were still working on 75 mW qualifications targeting production H2 2027. 

$SIVE has lower power 8/16 channel specs, and individual 200 mW lasers for NPO. I think this might relate to their Seminex partnership for UHP multi channel variants that they were targeting for 2027 so high confidence they'll meet technology specs eventually, more of a matter of timing. 

But basically new announced configuration from Ayar, can't really make any assumptions here yet, will need to wait for earnings of these players.

I mean it's probably more important to look at the actions over words... I'm sure $GOOGL trying to secure supply until 2035, would spark other hyperscalers to follow suit as well. 

They probably wouldn't be going 9 years out if they thought there would be overflooding in supply from China in 2 years.

Glad we finally got a word too from $NVDA Jensen Huang today from an event at Stockholm...

About $CRWV amid the broader Neocloud selloff. 

When asked about the markets reactions to Coreweave, Jensen responded: 

- "Coreweave's strength is improving every day, I'm optimistic"
- "The cost of capital is actually decreasing"

On whether Nvidia needed to provide a financial backstop:

- Jensen said he did not see a need for Nvidia to backstop CoreWeave

I'm personally not too positive about $CRWV relative to $NBIS and the others... but any copium helps from the man himself with market sentiment.
